comparison.objective: Candidate adjusts and locks a robot gripper’s opening stop at 90° and verifies retained actuation; PR-757 strips 8–12 mm of insulation from a cable using a lever-operated benchtop station.
comparison.physical_skill: Candidate requires coaxial driver and thin-wrench seating, coupled screw–jam-nut countertorque, setting preservation, tool withdrawal, and articulated cycling. PR-757 requires depth-controlled cable insertion, sustained lever depression against spring/cutting force, and straight cable extraction while the blades remain closed.
comparison.success_condition: Candidate scores angular accuracy, nut retention, limited stop drift across three cycles, and one-second hands-off clearance, with loss revocation. PR-757 scores insertion progress, completed stripping length, lever release, and gripper clearance, with explicit cut/pull force checks in its latest version.
comparison.reason: The tasks share bimanual force coordination and release verification only at a generic level; one tests preserving a precision mechanical adjustment during locknut tightening and subsequent cyclic retention, while the other tests cable positioning and material removal under a held cutting mechanism.
